summary: 彼得·贝克把少年时代造火箭的愿望变成了新西兰的 Rocket Lab。文章串起家庭工坊、学徒工作、投资者与当地支持者的帮助，以及首次发射如何为后续商业航天合同建立信誉。
logic: 为什么在新西兰创业并选择发射场
童年对太空的兴趣与技术学徒生涯
寻找早期合伙人、资金与支持
从承接航天合同到规划自己的发射业务
小型卫星市场、投资与家乡的支持

paragraphs.brief: 你的童年梦想在你的后院并不常成真尤其是如果你的梦想是向太空发射火箭的话
sentences: It’s not often your boyhood dream comes true in your own backyard, especially if your dream is to blast rockets into space.
你的童年梦想在你的后院并不常成真尤其是如果你的梦想是向太空发射火箭的话
Think of such things and your mind probably goes to NASA or Russia or perhaps one of those barren-looking launch pads in a dusty Middle-Eastern landscape.
想想这些事情，你的心思可能去美国航天局或俄罗斯或者也许一个荒凉的发射台在灰尘的中东景观。
Or Thunderbirds and their mysterious tropical island.
或者是雷鸟以及他们神秘的热带岛

paragraphs.brief: 但星星已经向南兰德和火箭爱好者彼得·贝克倾斜了
sentences: But the stars have turned favourably for Southlander and rocket enthusiast Peter Beck.
但星星已经向南兰德和火箭爱好者彼得·贝克倾斜了

paragraphs.brief: 如果世界上发射火箭的最好地方是在沙漠的中间那就是我所在的地方就这么简单了
sentences: “If the best place in the world to launch rockets was in the middle of a desert that’s where I’d be – it’s that simple.
如果世界上发射火箭的最好地方是在沙漠的中间那就是我所在的地方就这么简单了
But it turns out that launching satellites into space is best done from right here, in New Zealand.”
但事实证明，向太空发射卫星最好从新西兰这里开始。”

paragraphs.brief: 这是一个快乐的巧合，因为基维火箭的先驱，他吸引了全球对似乎像兔子脑计划的投资，他只想做一件事：发射火箭和许多火箭。
sentences: Now that is a happy coincidence, because the Kiwi rocket pioneer, who has attracted global investment into what seems like a hare-brained scheme, wants to do just one thing: launch rockets and lots of them.
这是一个快乐的巧合，因为基维火箭的先驱，他吸引了全球对似乎像兔子脑计划的投资，他只想做一件事：发射火箭和许多火箭。
Always has.
总是这样

paragraphs.brief: 很快我们就会知道他的火箭实验室打算在哪里建造发射设施
sentences: Soon we’ll know exactly where his company Rocket Lab plans to build its launch facility.
很快我们就会知道他的火箭实验室打算在哪里建造发射设施
The best guesses are somewhere remote in the South Island.
最好的猜测是在南岛的偏僻地方
On reflection, it’s an obvious location.
反省一下，这是一个明显的地点。

paragraphs.brief: 所以新西兰在荒郊野外的小岛屿国家的唯一优势是，如果你想发射火箭。
sentences: “When we shoot, there’s nothing there: no air traffic, no population, no shipping, just nothing.
我们开枪时，那里什么都没有：没有空中交通，没有人口，没有航运，只是一无所有。
In America, if you said you wanted to launch a satellite once a week they’d laugh at you because there’s shipping, there’s a ton of flights, there’s people, there’s everything everywhere.
在美国，如果你说你想每周发射一次卫星，他们会嘲笑你，因为有船运，有一吨的航班，有人民，到处都有。
So New Zealand’s only advantage of being a small island nation in the middle of nowhere is if you want to launch rockets.
所以新西兰在荒郊野外的小岛屿国家的唯一优势是，如果你想发射火箭。
It’s perfect!”
」 英文译者：

paragraphs.brief: 即使我在其中一个组织里做了真正大的事情，我还是不会做我想做的事 — — 发射火箭。
sentences: Perfect wasn’t always how Beck described it.
贝克的描述并不总是那么完美。
When he packed his bags in 2007 for the trip of a lifetime to NASA and Lockheed Martin he discovered not the labs of his boyhood dreams but an industry moribund in bureaucracy and spiralling costs.
当他于2007年收拾行李前往美国航天局和洛克希德·马丁的一生之旅时，他发现了的不是他童年梦想的实验室而是一个行业在官僚主义和螺旋式成本上的萎缩。
“I started talking to these guys and they go ‘You don’t want to work here’.
我开始和这些家伙谈话他们就说"你不想在这里工作"
I realised that I was just going to be a tiny gear in a giant bureaucratic machine.
我意识到，我只是想成为一个小齿轮在巨大的官僚机器。
And even if I made it really really big in one of these organisations then I was still not going to do what I wanted – launch rockets.”
即使我在其中一个组织里做了真正大的事情，我还是不会做我想做的事 — — 发射火箭。

paragraphs.brief: “我当时想，“哇，这是我童年的梦想，只是没有跨越。”
sentences: Depressed, he caught a plane home.
沮丧的是，他坐飞机回家。
“I was, like, ‘Wow, this is my childhood dream and it’s just not panning out’.”
“我当时想，“哇，这是我童年的梦想，只是没有跨越。”

paragraphs.brief: “大约六个月后，我辞去工作，开始建造火箭实验室，就是这样。”
sentences: But they make kids tough in Southland.
但他们让南边的孩子变得很坚强
And disobedient too.
并且不听话
Aboard the flight, he Googled a company name and designed a logo and registered his company as soon as he landed.
登机后，他用谷歌搜索了一个公司名称，设计了一个标志，并在他着陆后立即登记了他的公司。
“About six months later I quit my job and started Rocketlab and that was that.”
“大约六个月后，我辞去工作，开始建造火箭实验室，就是这样。”

paragraphs.brief: 该公司声称，它最终将处理每年100次发射。
sentences: He makes it sound so easy.
听起来很简单
By the end of this year, Beck plans to send his first payload into space, just the second non-government funded company ever to do so.
到今年年底，贝克计划将他的第一颗有效载荷送入太空，这是第二家非政府资助的公司。
After that, he says, there are 30 or so customers lined up to launch their small satellites.
之后，他说，有大约30个客户排队发射他们的小型卫星。
Plans are for one launch a month in 2016, and then one a week in 2017.
计划在2016年每月一次启动，2017年每周一次。
The company claims it will eventually handle 100 launches a year.
该公司声称，它最终将处理每年100次发射。

paragraphs.brief: 以500万美元一针，生意可能是一个爆炸性。
sentences: “Space is open for business,” Beck says.
贝克说，“空间对商业开放”。
And at $US5 million a shot, business could be a blast.
以500万美元一针，生意可能是一个爆炸性。

paragraphs.role: 特派团可能采取的行动
paragraphs.brief: 贝克用他像小天使一样的脸，毛发和无间断的发型，勾勾了所有疯狂科学家的箱子。
sentences: With his cherub-like face, frizzy hair and uninterruptible patter, Beck ticks all the boxes of the mad scientist.
贝克用他像小天使一样的脸，毛发和无间断的发型，勾勾了所有疯狂科学家的箱子。
Plus there’s the impatience of a man on a mission.
再加上执行任务的人的不耐烦。

paragraphs.brief: 人们只是不看不够，他栏杆。
sentences: People just don’t look up enough, he rails.
人们只是不看不够，他栏杆。
“I’m constantly surprised at how little people understand where they live.
我不断感到惊讶的是很少有人知道他们住在哪里。
They might say ‘I live in this suburb in this city and in this country’ but nobody thinks of themselves as living in a solar system.
他们可能会说"我住在这个郊区在这个城市和这个国家" 但没有人认为自己生活在太阳系里
If you ask the average person to name the planets, they can’t.
如果你问普通人命名行星，他们不能。
I mean, can you?”
我是说，你能吗？”

paragraphs.brief: “好吧，这样你也许知道的比大多数人更多，尽管你把订单弄错了。”
sentences: It sounds like a test so I rattle off all the planets I can remember (“Pluto’s not a planet, it’s a ball of ice!”
听起来像是个测试所以我就把记忆中所有的行星都打乱了 (“冥王星不是行星，是冰球! ”
I say, remembering something from the news) and Beck looks slightly disappointed.
我说，记得一些新闻) 贝克看起来有点失望。
“Okay so you might know more than most, though you got the order wrong.”
“好吧，这样你也许知道的比大多数人更多，尽管你把订单弄错了。”

paragraphs.brief: 对38岁的孩子来说，这很重要
sentences: Space matters.
空间问题。
And it has mattered a long time for the 38-year-old.
对38岁的孩子来说，这很重要

paragraphs.brief: 他的父亲罗素(Russell)在18岁时为南地博物馆建造了一台大型望远镜(仍在使用)。
sentences: Beck built his own telescope as a child, following the example of his father Russell, who constructed a large telescope for the Southland museum when he was just 18 (it’s still in use).
他的父亲罗素(Russell)在18岁时为南地博物馆建造了一台大型望远镜(仍在使用)。

Russell later became the museum director and Peter remembers “at about six or seven going to stuffy old Astronomical Society meetings at the museum where you’ve got all these boffins sitting around drinking tea talking about space and telescopes.
罗素后来成为了博物馆的馆长彼得记得 "大约六七天天文学会在博物馆开会" "在那里你坐着这么多的松饼喝着茶谈论太空和望远镜"
A lot of these guys had PhDs and really knew their stuff.
很多人有博士学位并真正了解他们的东西。
I found it absolutely fascinating and probably understood 5% of what was being said.
我发现它绝对令人着迷并且大概能理解5%的话
But I was hooked.”
但我上瘾了。”

paragraphs.brief: 所有那些话本可以让贝克成为一名学者，但他却在家庭工作坊中弄脏了手脚，他带着激情与祖父一起，他祖父将借工具给另一个著名的南边工匠《世界最快的印度名声》的伯特·蒙罗。
sentences: All that talk could have made Beck an academic but he got his hands dirty in the family workshop, carrying on a passion that started with his grandfather who would lend tools to another famous Southland tinkerer, Burt Munro of The World’s Fastest Indian fame.
所有那些话本可以让贝克成为一名学者，但他却在家庭工作坊中弄脏了手脚，他带着激情与祖父一起，他祖父将借工具给另一个著名的南边工匠《世界最快的印度名声》的伯特·蒙罗。
“Burt used to come into my grandfather’s workshop and use his equipment and make a hell of a mess and leave,” Beck says.
贝克说：“伯特过去常来我祖父的车间使用他的设备弄得一团糟然后离开。”

paragraphs.brief: David表哥仍经营着Beck Industries，这是Peter叔叔Doug所开的工程商店。
sentences: Engineering runs in the family.
工程是一家人经营的
Before the museum Peter’s dad, Russell, was an engineer.
在彼得的父亲罗素之前是个工程师
Peter’s middle brother Andrew is a mechanical engineer and electrician; his oldest brother John runs a caryard by day and is a competitive motorcyclist in the weekend.
Peter的中兄弟Andrew是一名机械工程师和电工；他的老兄弟John白天经营一个汽车厂，周末是具有竞争力的摩托车手。
Cousin David still runs Beck Industries, the engineering shop set up by Peter’s uncle Doug.
David表哥仍经营着Beck Industries，这是Peter叔叔Doug所开的工程商店。
Their speciality: outdoor vacuum cleaners.
他们的专长是室外吸尘器

paragraphs.brief: 家庭车库是男孩们建造卡通车的地方，然后，在他们十几岁的时候，他们把迷你车弄得一团糟。
sentences: The family garage was where the boys built go-karts and then, in their teenage years, souped up their Minis.
家庭车库是男孩们建造卡通车的地方，然后，在他们十几岁的时候，他们把迷你车弄得一团糟。
“They all modified our Minis,” recalls Russell.
“他们都改造了我们的迷你，”罗素记得。
“They’re easy to work on and actually pretty much anything you do improves them.
“他们很容易工作，实际上，你所做的任何事情都会改善他们。
Peter was determined to make his go faster.”
Peter决心要加快速度。”

paragraphs.brief: 我对我想做的事太明确了测试也不允许
sentences: “It’s always been about the rocket, there’s never been a question really – even at high school.
一直以来都是关于火箭从来没有一个真正的问题甚至在高中的时候
I remember I failed a careers assessment test and they needed to talk to my parents about it.
我记得我考了职业评估考失败了他们需要跟我父母谈谈
I was so defined about what I wanted to do and the test didn’t allow for that.”
我对我想做的事太明确了测试也不允许

paragraphs.brief: 在因弗卡尔吉尔的James Hargest学院，这一趋势仍在继续，那里的金属制工教师“把他带到车间的钥匙上”(David说)，然后在Dunedin的Fisher & Paykel，他在那里完成了工具制造学徒工作，并学习了“如何将工程和设计结合起来”。
sentences: The trend continued at James Hargest College in Invercargill, where the metalwork teacher “threw him the keys to the workshop” (says David) and then at Dunedin’s Fisher & Paykel, where he completed a tool-making apprenticeship and learned (says Russell) “how to combine engineering and design.
在因弗卡尔吉尔的James Hargest学院，这一趋势仍在继续，那里的金属制工教师“把他带到车间的钥匙上”(David说)，然后在Dunedin的Fisher & Paykel，他在那里完成了工具制造学徒工作，并学习了“如何将工程和设计结合起来”。
He’s very precise – everything always has to work and look good, with Peter.”
他非常精确 — — 与彼得在一起，每件事都要工作，看起来都很好。

paragraphs.brief: 也是在2000年，在F&P的同事的慷慨帮助下，他建造了一辆火箭驱动的自行车，他用在Dunedin's Princess街的140公里的爆炸向公众展示了。
sentences: It’s also where, in 2000, with generous help from his colleagues at F&P, he built a rocket-powered bicycle that he demonstrated to the bemused public with a 140 kph blast down Dunedin’s Princes Street.
也是在2000年，在F&P的同事的慷慨帮助下，他建造了一辆火箭驱动的自行车，他用在Dunedin's Princess街的140公里的爆炸向公众展示了。

paragraphs.brief: 当我进入一个设计角色时，我对火箭喷嘴进行了模拟，优化了火箭燃料的流动。”
sentences: “At F&P they would give me lumps of titanium and just write them off as apprentice-training projects.
“在F&P公司，他们会给我一整块钛，然后把它们当作学徒培训项目来注销。
I’d build my rockets at night using their workshops.
我晚上会用他们的车间制造火箭。
And when I moved into a design role I did simulations on rocket nozzles, optimising the flow for rocket fuels.”
当我进入一个设计角色时，我对火箭喷嘴进行了模拟，优化了火箭燃料的流动。”

paragraphs.brief: 接着，贝克在奥克兰帕内尔的工业研究有限公司(现已并入卡拉汉创新公司)找到一份工作，他在那里深入了解金属及其优势，并学习了如何测试他的想法。
sentences: Next, Beck landed a job at Industrial Research Ltd in Parnell, Auckland (now merged into Callaghan Innovation), where he developed a deep understanding of metals and their strengths, and learned how to test his ideas.
接着，贝克在奥克兰帕内尔的工业研究有限公司(现已并入卡拉汉创新公司)找到一份工作，他在那里深入了解金属及其优势，并学习了如何测试他的想法。
And his rockets.
还有他的火箭
As at F&P, IRL managers turned a beneficent blind eye to his after-hours experiments.
与F&P一样，IRL管理人员对下班后的实验视而不见。

paragraphs.brief: 我对我想做的事太明确了测试也不允许
sentences: “It’s always been about the rocket, there’s never been a question really – even at high school.
一直以来都是关于火箭从来没有一个真正的问题甚至在高中的时候
I remember I failed a careers assessment test and they needed to talk to my parents about it.
我记得我考了职业评估考失败了他们需要跟我父母谈谈
I was so defined about what I wanted to do and the test didn’t allow for that.”
我对我想做的事太明确了测试也不允许

paragraphs.brief: 人们常开玩笑说：“还是干好你的本职工作吧。”
sentences: “Stick to the day job,” the joke goes.
人们常开玩笑说：“还是干好你的本职工作吧。”
That’s good advice for most of us.
这对我们大多数人都是好建议。
But when Beck quit his job he attracted more than the usual bunch of family and fools.
但是当贝克辞职时他吸引了比平时更多的家人和傻瓜

paragraphs.brief: 很多人对事物有激情却没跟上来
sentences: “Lots of people have passion for things and don’t follow through.
很多人对事物有激情却没跟上来
Peter’s passion is rockets – but he’s also got the engineering skills.
Peter的热情是火箭，但他也拥有工程技能。
He can see it through.”
他能够看穿。”

paragraphs.brief: 这是艾伦・约翰斯顿，建筑经理 IRL的Balfour St房地，谁肩并肩年轻企业家占据空位在二楼。
sentences: That’s Alan Johnston, the building manager of IRL’s Balfour St premises, who shoulder-tapped the young entrepreneur to occupy empty space on the second floor.
这是艾伦・约翰斯顿，建筑经理 IRL的Balfour St房地，谁肩并肩年轻企业家占据空位在二楼。
“There weren’t many places in Auckland that young entrepreneurs could go for this kind of hi-tech manufacturing.
奥克兰没有太多地方让青年企业家去从事这种高科技制造业。
So I charged him a low rent and allowed him to use the equipment, especially the labs.
所以我给他低价租金并允许他使用设备特别是实验室
I didn’t really ask permission from HQ.
我并没有真正向总部申请许可。
It just seemed like the right thing to do.”
这似乎是正确的事情。”

paragraphs.brief: 早期支持者还有互联网企业家、太空迷马克·罗基特。他通过正式法律手续把名字从马克·史蒂文斯改为现在的名字，还因成为第一位参加维珍银河太空旅游计划的新西兰人而受到媒体报道。
sentences: Another early supporter was Mark Rocket, the internet entrepreneur and space-nut who changed his name by deed poll from Mark Stevens and received media coverage as the first Kiwi to join Virgin Galactic’s space tourism programme.
早期支持者还有互联网企业家、太空迷马克·罗基特。他通过正式法律手续把名字从马克·史蒂文斯改为现在的名字，还因成为第一位参加维珍银河太空旅游计划的新西兰人而受到媒体报道。
Beck approached Rocket and the two hit it off, with the latter adding seed capital and becoming a 50% owner until he exited in 2011.
Beck接近火箭，两枚火箭击中了火箭，后者增加了种子资本，成为50%的拥有者，直至2011年他退出。

paragraphs.brief: 我们和中央政府谈过了他们总是倒着走过来帮我们
sentences: “Everyone is rooting for us.
“每个人都在为我们扎根。
I think it’s very Kiwi that no matter who we talk to, everybody is rooting for us and wants us to succeed.
不论我们和谁交谈，所有人都支持我们并希望我们成功。
And you know, we talked to Civil Aviation and they bent over backwards to help us.
我们跟民航公司谈过了他们倒着过来帮我们
We talked to central Government and they’ve always bent over backwards and helped us.”
我们和中央政府谈过了他们总是倒着走过来帮我们

paragraphs.brief: 我建议，这种支持是不寻常的。
sentences: I suggest that it’s unusual, this kind of support.
我建议，这种支持是不寻常的。

paragraphs.brief: 这是真实的真相从我们试图建造发射场的城市的市长们向所有人说
sentences: “Really?”
“真的吗？”
Beck asks.
贝克问。
“Well, it’s the honest truth and anywhere from the mayors of the cities where we’re trying to build launch sites, to well anybody.
这是真实的真相从我们试图建造发射场的城市的市长们向所有人说
We’ve never ever hit a brick wall from any regulators or people in power.”
我们从未打过任何管理者或掌权者的砖墙。

paragraphs.brief: 2009年11月30日下午2点28分，TV3播放了“Tea-1”号火箭原型的少女飞行。
sentences: The support came to a dramatic, and media-propelled, climax at 2:28pm on November 30, 2009, when TV3 broadcast the maiden flight of Ātea-1, Rocket Lab’s prototype rocket.
2009年11月30日下午2点28分，TV3播放了“Tea-1”号火箭原型的少女飞行。
After technical delays (including a dash to a local mechanic) Ātea, also named Manu Karere, blasted into a clear sky.
经历技术故障造成的延误（其间还急忙找过当地机械师）后，另名“马努·卡雷雷”的“阿泰阿”号终于升入晴空。

paragraphs.brief: 2011年写了马克·火箭：“这是一个惊人的景象和声音以观察。”
sentences: “It was an amazing sight and sound to behold,” wrote Mark Rocket in 2011.
2011年写了马克·火箭：“这是一个惊人的景象和声音以观察。”
“The rocket flew beautifully and powerfully into the sky, the throaty roar of the hybrid rocket engine reverberating over the island.
“火箭飞向天空时美丽而有力，混合火箭发动机的喉咙在岛上回荡。
The spectators were elated and tears of joy erupted.
观众欢欣鼓舞，欢乐的泪水爆发。
Some were crying from the drama of the day’s events and the profoundness of the experience.”
有些人对当日事件和经历的深刻性哭泣。

paragraphs.brief: 贝克在电视上像疯子一样跳着喊叫
sentences: Beck can be seen leaping and yelling like a loon on the TV footage.
贝克在电视上像疯子一样跳着喊叫

paragraphs.brief: 火箭实验室接待处的那位好女士说我无法在大楼里拿手机
sentences: The nice lady at the Rocket Lab reception says I can’t carry my cell-phone in the building.
火箭实验室接待处的那位好女士说我无法在大楼里拿手机
“Top secret,” she says.
她说，这是“绝密”。
“But take a seat, there’s a new Woman’s Day there.”
但请坐，那里有一个新的妇女节。

paragraphs.brief: 最初发射六年后，奥克兰机场附近的混凝土办公室几乎不像一个开拓性卫星公司的总部。
sentences: Six years after that initial launch, and the bland, concrete office near Auckland’s airport hardly looks like the HQ of a pioneering satellite company.
最初发射六年后，奥克兰机场附近的混凝土办公室几乎不像一个开拓性卫星公司的总部。
I imagine that in the US, something like Rocket Lab would be barricaded with heavy fences and heavier guards.
我想在美国火箭实验室之类的东西会被围着重的栅栏和更重的守卫
A reporter from a no-name magazine would certainly have trouble getting access to its boss.
一个无名杂志的记者肯定很难接触到它的老板
In New Zealand you just pick up the phone.
在新西兰，你只要接电话。

paragraphs.brief: 这让火箭实验室的成功更加引人注目。
sentences: It makes Rocket Lab’s success all the more remarkable.
这让火箭实验室的成功更加引人注目。

paragraphs.brief: 当时只有三名工作人员(2010年)，火箭实验室与国际公司签订了航空航天工作合同。
sentences: With just three staff at the time (2010), Rocket Lab won contracts with international firms for aerospace work.
当时只有三名工作人员(2010年)，火箭实验室与国际公司签订了航空航天工作合同。

In particular from DARPA, the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, which is attributed with the invention of technologies such as GPS, the CDMA cell phone network and ARPANET, the precursor of the internet.
特别是美国国防高级研究项目局，该局发明了全球定位系统、CDMA手机网络和ARPANET等技术，这是互联网的前身。
Beck won’t say what Rocket Lab worked on, but the money flowed and the credibility built, along with the staff.
贝克不会说火箭实验室的工作，但钱流和信誉建立，与工作人员一起。

paragraphs.brief: 到了2011年，我感到我们已经到了这个行业有足够的信誉去做我真正想做的事。
sentences: “By 2011, I sort of felt that we’d reached the point where we had enough credibility within the industry to do what I really wanted.
到了2011年，我感到我们已经到了这个行业有足够的信誉去做我真正想做的事。
It was kind of a crossroads, because we could have gone down the aerospace contractor road but I’m absolutely negatively inspired by doing that.”
这是一种十字路口，因为我们本可以走航空航天承包商的道路，但我绝对消极的灵感这样做。

paragraphs.brief: 所以他又撞上了画板设计了Eletron的图案他希望火箭能支撑发射业务
sentences: So he hit the drawing board again and laid plans for Electron, the rocket that he hopes will underpin the launch business.
所以他又撞上了画板设计了Eletron的图案他希望火箭能支撑发射业务

paragraphs.brief: “他的胆识打动了我。”The Warehouse 创始人斯蒂芬·廷德尔说。2013 年 10 月，他的 K1W1 基金与政府机构卡拉汉创新中心一起进行了投资。
sentences: Again, the tributes and support flowed.
悼念和支持再次涌现。
“I was inspired by his audacity,” says Warehouse founder Stephen Tindall, whose K1W1 fund invested in October 2013, along with the Government’s Callaghan Innovation.
“他的胆识打动了我。”The Warehouse 创始人斯蒂芬·廷德尔说。2013 年 10 月，他的 K1W1 基金与政府机构卡拉汉创新中心一起进行了投资。

paragraphs.brief: 受启发的还有太阳微系统共同创始人维诺德·霍斯拉，也是硅谷最受尊敬的风险资本家之一。
sentences: Also inspired was Vinod Khosla, co-founder of Sun Microsystems and one of Silicon Valley’s most respected venture capitalists.
受启发的还有太阳微系统共同创始人维诺德·霍斯拉，也是硅谷最受尊敬的风险资本家之一。
Khosla’s investment provided not just much-needed capital, but global credibility.
霍斯拉的投资不仅提供了急需的资本，而且提供了全球信誉。

paragraphs.brief: 对小型卫星公司来说，发射是最困难的事情。”
sentences: “We were kind of lucky with Khosla in the fact that they had previously invested in [micro-satellite Company] Sky Box, sold last year to Google.
我们很幸运地与Khosla合作，因为他们以前投资过去年卖给谷歌的(微型卫星公司)Sky Box。
So they had experienced firsthand the issues of getting a small satellite in orbit.
因此，他们亲身体验到在轨道上获得一颗小型卫星的问题。
Launch is the single hardest thing for small satellite companies.”
对小型卫星公司来说，发射是最困难的事情。”

paragraphs.brief: 每年有几十个卫星发射，但Khosla对一个老问题的新办法却很感动。
sentences: There are dozens of satellite launches every year but what appealed to Khosla was the new approach to an old problem.
每年有几十个卫星发射，但Khosla对一个老问题的新办法却很感动。
So far most of the commercial effort has gone into satellite technology, with only a handful of companies, including Richard Branson’s Virgin Galactic, reinventing launch.
迄今为止，大多数商业努力都投入到卫星技术中，只有少数公司，包括理查德·布兰森的维尔京银河系，正在重新发明发射。
“What’s normally done in this industry is that you take a heritage Russian rocket motor from here, and a heritage tank from over there, and you put them all together.
通常在这个行业，你从这里拿走俄罗斯传统火箭发动机，从那边取出一个传统坦克，把它们放在一起。
But to start from scratch and assume there are no constraints is a new approach.”
但是，从零开始，假设没有任何限制是新的办法。”

paragraphs.brief: 从这个意义上讲，新西兰是火箭实验室成功的一部分。
sentences: In that sense, the New Zealand-ness is part of Rocket Lab’s success.
从这个意义上讲，新西兰是火箭实验室成功的一部分。
A country with no heritage in space is exactly where you’d expect ground-breaking innovation to come from.
一个没有空间遗产的国家正是你期待突破性创新来自的地方。
Khosla’s other investments in New Zealand are similar outliers: Lanzatech, the waste-to-energy company started by Sean Simpson, and Biodiscovery NZ, a biotech company extracting plant microbes.
Khosla在新西兰的其他投资也是类似的外部投资：由Sean Simpson创办的废物换能源公司Lanzatech和一家生物技术公司Biodiscovery NZ，一家采掘植物微生物的公司。

paragraphs.brief: 新西兰的碳纤维、可回收火箭、双电/干燃料发动机、秘密带电子产品和端对端发射设施的组合意味着贝克估计他可以将发射价格从1.3亿美元降至490万美元。
sentences: Rocket Lab’s solution, the Electron, is novel.
火箭实验室的解决方案“电子”是新奇的。

The combination of a carbon-fibre, recoverable rocket, a dual electric/dry fuel engine, secret-sauce electronics and an end-to-end launch facility in New Zealand means Beck reckons he can slash the price of launch from about $US130 million to $US4.9 million.
新西兰的碳纤维、可回收火箭、双电/干燃料发动机、秘密带电子产品和端对端发射设施的组合意味着贝克估计他可以将发射价格从1.3亿美元降至490万美元。
That saving means the much-hyped shift from government-dominated space travel to industry-led might finally happen.
这种节约意味着从政府主导的空间旅行向产业主导的转变可能最终会发生。

paragraphs.brief: 今年3月，火箭实验室进行了第二轮正式筹资，即B系列，说服Khosla和K1W1再投资。
sentences: The Electron keeps winning impressive support.
电子公司一直赢得令人印象深刻的支持。
In March this year, Rocket Lab conducted its second formal funding round, Series B, convincing Khosla and K1W1 to reinvest.
今年3月，火箭实验室进行了第二轮正式筹资，即B系列，说服Khosla和K1W1再投资。

It also added two industry heavyweights: Bessemer Venture Partners, one of the oldest venture capital firms in the world (and the money men behind global success stories such as Staples, International Paper, Skype and Shopify); and Lockheed Martin, major supplier to military and space programmes.
它还增加了两个工业重量级公司：Bessemer风险投资伙伴公司，这是世界上最古老的风险资本公司之一(以及Staples、国际纸报、Skype和Shoppy等全球成功故事背后的货币人);以及Lockheed Martin，军事和空间方案的主要供应商。

paragraphs.brief: 他说洛克希德的新闻稿：“火箭实验室的工作可以应用于一些航空航天领域，我们期待着与它们合作，以补充我们在小型升降能力和超音速飞行技术方面的总体努力。”
sentences: “Rocket Lab’s work could have application in a number of aerospace domains and we look forward to working with them to complement our overall efforts in small lift capabilities and hypersonic flight technologies,” says Lockheed’s press release.
他说洛克希德的新闻稿：“火箭实验室的工作可以应用于一些航空航天领域，我们期待着与它们合作，以补充我们在小型升降能力和超音速飞行技术方面的总体努力。”

paragraphs.brief: 贝克认为投资的到来是因为市场已经准备好了
sentences: Beck believes the investment comes because the market is ready.
贝克认为投资的到来是因为市场已经准备好了
“In the next decade you’re going to see space change from being a government-controlled domain, to commercial.
未来十年，你会看到空间从政府控制的域域变为商业域。
It’s government railroad versus FedEx vans.
政府铁路对FedEx面包车。
It’s just awesome.”
” 说得好,

paragraphs.brief: 但是，这种支持也反映了一个荒谬的梦想。
sentences: But the support also reflects a ridiculous dream.
但是，这种支持也反映了一个荒谬的梦想。

From its early days as a cheap tenant in Balfour Street to its current 50 or so international staff, Rocket Lab is a testament to Beck’s passion and skill – and a textbook example of how it takes a village to raise a child.
从Balfour街的廉价租户早期到目前约50名国际职员，火箭实验室证明了贝克的热情和技巧 — — 以及需要村庄抚养孩子的教科书范例。

paragraphs.brief: 从一个鼓励在工作坊玩耍的祖父到宽容的雇主和热情的业余人士，从直升机、媒体工作人员到厨师，从奥特亚罗亚到太空的旅程可能对我们来说是一条路。
sentences: From a grandfather who encouraged play in his workshop, to tolerant employers and enthusiastic amateurs giving money, helicopters, media crews and chefs, the journey to space from Aotearoa might be one for us.
从一个鼓励在工作坊玩耍的祖父到宽容的雇主和热情的业余人士，从直升机、媒体工作人员到厨师，从奥特亚罗亚到太空的旅程可能对我们来说是一条路。

points: 彼得·贝克把少年时代造火箭的愿望变成了新西兰的 Rocket Lab。文章串起家庭工坊、学徒工作、投资者与当地支持者的帮助，以及首次发射如何为后续商业航天合同建立信誉。
新西兰发射地点与商业设想 → 家庭工坊与技术学徒经历 → 寻找合作者和资金 → 首次成功发射 → 承接航天项目
clauses: It’s not often your boyhood dream comes true in your own backyard, ….
连接词 if 引出“especially if your dream is to blast rockets into space”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
“that launching satellites into space is best done from right here, in New Zealand”补足 turns 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 turns 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Peter Beck, CEO of commercial space race leader Rocket Lab, says he can send your satellite into space for just US$50,000 (NZ$76,000), and just as easily as booking an airline ticket.
商业太空竞赛领队火箭实验室的首席执行官Peter Beck说，他可以把你的卫星送进太空，只要5万美元(76,000新西兰元)，而且同样容易订机票。
Space, it seems, is now open for business.
